Subject: POC night soak — temporary quota ask

Hi Vanessa / Marissa,

Thanks again for the quick demo yesterday. We want to run a focused night-time soak this Friday to validate tail-latency under sustained concurrency (10k reqs/min sustained for 2 hours) as part of our POC. Our infra team asked if Redwood can provision an ephemeral capacity bridge — roughly equivalent to an extra 150k tokens and elevated concurrency headroom for the window — to avoid throttling during the run.

Attached is the soak plan and expected request profile (poc-plan-night-soak.xlsx). Can you confirm if this is something Redwood can temporarily enable and what the approval path looks like? If procurement needs a reference or PO, loop us in and we’ll expedite.

Thanks,
Sarah

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the plan and the clear profile. We can support an ephemeral capacity bridge for the Friday window. Quick notes:

- We generally provision a timeboxed quota bump for POCs like this (48 hours max) tied to the account and deal.
- For the scale you listed (10k reqs/min for 2h), we recommend enabling prefix caching + a higher batching profile for the run — Marissa will propose the precise config.
- We need a short note from procurement or a PO to track spend for the bump; otherwise we can attach it to the existing trial authorization under ACM-4721 for internal approval.

I’ll route this to our approvals queue now. If Karithik approves the account-level endorsement we can flip the switch and confirm the exact token allowance and time window.

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai; Sarah Tan <sarah.tan@acme-data.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC night soak — temporary quota ask

Thanks Sarah — I dug into the profile and attached a short runbook + expected KV cache hit curves (kv-cache-metrics.pdf). High-level suggestions for the Friday soak:

- Enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (should reduce token spend by ~30–40%).
- Increase max batch size to 512 and set target latency SLO to 220ms for the window.
- Pre-warm three dedicated GPU workers in the east-us region one hour prior to start; those workers will carry the bulk of the steady throughput.

If we provision a 48-hour ephemeral uplift of 150k token units and the three-worker pre-warm, we expect to see minimal throttling and stable tail latency.

Attachments: poc-plan-night-soak.xlsx (spreadsheet), kv-cache-metrics.pdf (summary).

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
